title: The bow
hookLine: Antony tells a hunter: if you bend a bow too much, it breaks; so with monks
tomorrow: why does every new fire start with smoke in your eyes?

cards: Somebody posts a clip of a well known for it, serious person goofing off, and the comments fill up: wait, is this allowed? A desert saying has that same double take in it.
A hunter is out after game and comes upon Abba Antony, relaxing with the brothers. Laughing, easy, at rest. The hunter is shocked.
Aren't these the people who pray through the night? So here's the puzzle: why is the elder everyone talks about out here taking it easy?

teach.h: PUT AN ARROW IN YOUR BOW.
teach.b: Antony doesn't explain. He gives the hunter a job. Put an arrow in your bow, he says, and shoot.
Again, says Antony. He shoots again. And again.
Finally the hunter says it himself: if I keep bending my bow like this, it'll break. There's the answer.
Antony says, in the sense of the saying, it's the same with the work of God. If we stretch the brothers beyond measure, they'll soon break. Sometimes we have to come down and meet their needs.
The hunter goes away helped, and the brothers go home strengthened. Here's the part to tell a friend: Antony never gives a speech about rest.

The hunter teaches himself, with his own bow, something he already knew; he just hadn't known it applied to monks. And the puzzle's answer isn't that Antony has gone soft. A bow that's never bent sends no arrow.
A bow that's never let down snaps.
The point is the rhythm: bend, release, bend again. Yesterday Abba Joseph said become all flame.
Today Antony says don't snap. The desert keeps both, and doesn't seem worried that they pull against each other.

how: Christian monastic life builds rest into the day, with set times for prayer, work, meals and sleep, and this saying of Antony is one that is told to explain why.

o: a deep bow of the head before an elder
a weapon the monks used to hunt in the desert
rest as part of the work, so you don't break

p: shocked to see the monks at ease
put an arrow in your bow, and shoot

s: Antony gives the hunter a long talk about rest
he hands him a task: shoot, again, again. the hunter finds the answer in his own bow.
to the desert monks, any rest was a lapse
the popular picture. in this saying Antony is at ease with the brothers, and says why.
the saying ends with the brothers going home strengthened
the hunter leaves helped, and the brothers strengthened.

games.q: your coach adds a practice every single day before the championship, and the team is running on empty. what would Antony's bow say?
o: keep every practice; the tightest bow shoots farthest.
build in rest days, so nobody breaks before the final.
cancel the season; rest is what really matters.
games.why: Antony didn't stop the work. he said stretch people beyond measure and they break. bend, release, bend again.

practice: Let your shoulders drop and your hands go slack, a bowstring let down. Close your eyes, and don't try to pray hard or plan anything. Just let one part of you at a time stop holding on, until the sit ends.

wordCard.voice: The bow. Antony's picture of the spiritual life: bent for the work, let down to rest, or it breaks.

orig.note: Greek: bow, the hunter's weapon in the saying.

carryVoice: Keep this one: don't overbend the bow, because rest is part of the work, not a break from it. Talk soon.

sources.ref: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Apophthegmata Patrum), Antony 13
